startMoraleSteady.note: Starting morale of units with steadiness below steadyThreshold.

steadyThreshold.note: Units steadier than this start at startMoraleSteady.

routThreshold.note: A formed unit at or below this routs.

destroyedFraction.note: Below this strength a unit ceases to exist.

casualtyShock.unit: morale per 1% of starting strength lost
casualtyShock.note: Multiplied by the cause factor and the unit's steadiness. The prototype's value is 1, which needs about 66% casualties from frontal fire to rout a battalion. Raised to 3 as a plausibility correction (MODEL.md 11, change A): a line battalion now breaks after about 22% losses to frontal musketry, 16% to canister, 10% to close fire on a column; a guard battalion stands half as much again. Anchor: units of the period usually gave way with a minority of their men down. Restore the prototype with --set data:morale.casualtyShock=1.

shockFireFlank.note: Musketry taken in flank or rear by infantry.

shockColumnClose.note: Musketry taken by a column inside columnCloseRange. This is what stops columns in front of a steady line.

artilleryCrewFactor.note: Gun crews lose half the morale other troops would for the same loss.

rippleRadius.note: 175 px x1.4. Reaches the neighbouring battalions in line and the supports behind, not the next but one.

rippleFriend.note: Lost by each friend within the radius when a unit routs or is destroyed; multiplied by steadiness.

rippleEnemy.note: Gained by each enemy within the radius.

squareSteadyMorale.note: A formed square at or above this is steady and repels cavalry.

contactCavOnForming.note: Infantry struck by cavalry while changing formation.

contactCavFront.note: Infantry not in square struck frontally by cavalry.

contactCavOnShakenSquare.note: A square below squareSteadyMorale when cavalry arrives.

contactSquareRepulse.note: Lost by cavalry that recoils from a steady square.

contactBayonet.note: Lost by a unit when a moving column reaches it.

recoveryDelay.note: Time without loss before recovery starts (5 s x7).

recoveryCapBase.note: Recovery ceiling is 100 x (base + (1 - base) x strength fraction).

routRecoveryRate.note: For a routed unit far from the enemy. The prototype's value divided by 7 is 0.86, which rallies a broken battalion in about half a minute and sends it straight back into the attack. Lowered as a plausibility correction (MODEL.md 11, change B): regaining the 28 points needed to rally now takes about nine minutes. Restore the prototype with --set data:morale.routRecoveryRate=0.86.

rallyMorale.note: A routed unit rallies on reaching this.

rallyEnemyDistance.note: No recovery or rally with a formed enemy nearer than this (250 px x1.4).

armyBreakFraction.note: An army breaks when this share of its starting units is routed or gone.

aftermathDuration.note: The run continues this long after an army breaks so the pursuit is counted (14 s x7).

cavRecoilRange.note: Cavalry hit by a volley inside this range may recoil (60 px x1.4).

cavRecoilMorale.note: It recoils if its morale is below this.

frontArc.note: An attacker within this angle of the target's facing is in front (1.05 rad).

flankArc.note: Beyond the front arc and within this angle is the flank; beyond it is the rear (2.3 rad).

chainWindow.note: Reporting only: how far back a rout's list of causes looks. Does not affect outcomes.
